verdictStatement.summary: I tried to make this the fifth rejection and I could not. IR-EP12-01 is genuinely repaired and I confirmed the repair in BOTH directions with bytes I wrote myself: my own MD2 and MD3, written from ep12.review-independent.json's prose rather than copied from the candidate's battery, each exit 0 against check-evaluation-proof-v12.py with a banner BYTE-IDENTICAL to that checker's honest banner, and each exits 1 against v13 with twelve findings of which the only rule that fires is A-9, seven times, once per vector. Then I built the attack the brief asked for and went past it. SB-MD6 compares NO BINDING AT ALL — no seat, no accessor, no module, no originals table, no closure cell, no frame, no dunder, no introspection primitive of any kind, asserted programmatically over the region text — and discriminates purely by counting the ledger entries its own call produces, which is MD5's means, plus the fact that the guard drives its hidden window immediately after its visible one. Where the candidate's own MD5 routes only the commitment, SB-MD6 routes ALL THREE: measured against v13, exit 0, banner BYTE-IDENTICAL to the honest run's, --selftest SELFTEST-PASS, and my independent seat attribution reports the verdict, the commitment AND the preimage for 7 of 7 pinned vectors produced by check-c2.py, against 7 of 7 by check-c2-v4.py for the unmodified checker in the identical harness. THE GATE ITSELF IS ROUTED. And that is not a blocker, because it is exactly what the enforced, banner-printed SCOPE_STATEMENT says will happen. THE SCOPE IS A CHARACTERISATION AND NOT AN ENUMERATION IN DIFFERENT CLOTHES, and the test I applied is the one that convicted v12: does a reader who applies the published boundary draw a false conclusion? Under v12 the boundary said frame-or-cell and my regions read neither, so the reader was misled. Under v13 the boundary is a CAPABILITY — 'any route region that can DISTINGUISH A CALL THIS GUARD IS MEASURING FROM A CALL IT IS NOT, BY ANY MEANS WHATEVER, and that answers honestly whenever it judges itself observed' — with three named means explicitly demoted to instances, an anti-enumeration clause binding the whole document, and the sentence 'there are others this instrument has not thought of and cannot enumerate'. My strongest escape lands inside it and was predicted by it. Nothing I built escapes the boundary; everything I built confirms it. The honesty is ENFORCED rather than intended: MD5 is built and executed on every ordinary run, is in DECLARED_ESCAPES, and verify_evasion produces a finding IF IT IS EVER CAUGHT ('either the scope statement is understated or the variant no longer performs the discrimination it names'); dropping it from escapedEveryGuard or declaredBlindSpotVariants is rejected, and aNarrowingIsNotAClosure must be true. Every other claim the brief put to me held under execution: A-9 fails closed (39 findings when its window cannot be installed); the predecessor control now fails closed — I re-ran the v12 reviewer's exact attack and got 14 findings, and republishing the degraded block verbatim still gives 13, against v12's green run printing {'UNATTRIBUTED': 7}; --selftest is 75/75 and I broke it in both directions; residual anchors are load-bearing sentences and 19 of 19 vague-padding attacks plus 9 of my 10 anchor-damage attacks are rejected; my own float/bool sweep reproduces the published battery digit for digit (180 integer leaves, 198 cases, 4 admitted and they are EXACTLY the four published positions, 148 rejected by a position-naming finding, 46 by whole-block strict_equal, 0 by census arithmetic, no bool admitted anywhere); RES-EP13-11 correctly restates what v12 got wrong and I re-ran check-completeness.py to confirm both causes; every declared dependent exits 0 and the two declared failures fail for the declared reasons. WHERE I LAND ON THE TERMINUS: this is an acceptable terminus, and I say so as the reviewer who routed the gate. What remains open is six non-blocking observations, of which the sharpest is that two blocks the checker does NOT verify — assurance.nonClaims and guardInventory.whatNoGuardHereCovers — still carry the predecessor's narrow frame-or-cell framing and two counts of 'twenty-five' where this run builds and publishes twenty-nine. That is stale prose in unenforced fields, contradicted by the enforced scope's own override clause, and it is three edits from correct; it is not the v12 defect, because nothing in it claims the property IS established outside the named set.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: The scope statement — is the characterisation genuine, can it be narrowed, can the self-scan be defeated?
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: THE CHARACTERISATION IS GENUINE. The self-scan is real but WEAKER THAN CLAIMED, and it cannot detect narrowing at all. Neither weakness is blocking.
centralClaimAdjudications.theTestIApplied: The test that convicted v12 is: does a reader who applies the published boundary draw a FALSE conclusion? v12's boundary was 'a route region that reads or writes this guard's own stack frame, or the closure cells of the servers it installs: variants AX6, AX9 and RX2c', and two regions that read neither defeated it. So the reader was misled. v13's boundary is a CAPABILITY, not a spelling and not a list: 'NOT ESTABLISHED against any route region that can DISTINGUISH A CALL THIS GUARD IS MEASURING FROM A CALL IT IS NOT, BY ANY MEANS WHATEVER, and that answers honestly whenever it judges itself observed'. I then built the hardest region I could and asked whether the boundary covers it. It does — see claim 3. A reader applying v13's boundary excludes SB-MD6, excludes MD5, excludes MD2/MD3/MD4, excludes AX6/AX9/RX2c, and excludes classes nobody has built, because the boundary is stated by what the region can DO and not by what it names.
centralClaimAdjudications.whyItIsNotAnEnumerationInDifferentClothe: Four structural features, each of which I checked rather than took on trust. (a) The class is defined by capability in the sentence that carries the word THEREFORE, and the three means that follow are introduced as 'ONE means', 'a SECOND' and 'a THIRD' and closed with 'there are others this instrument has not thought of and cannot enumerate'. (b) There is an explicit anti-enumeration clause binding the WHOLE document: 'EVERY VARIANT NAMED ANYWHERE IN THIS DOCUMENT IS AN INSTANCE OF THAT CLASS AND IS NEVER ITS DEFINITION, and no set, count, matrix or enumeration published here — including escapedEveryGuard, and including the variants A-9 is measured catching — may be read as bounding it.' (c) It states its own incompleteness as a positive measured fact rather than a caveat: A-9 is 'a NARROWING, NOT A CLOSURE', and 'a region reaching the same class by a means A-9 does not remove is built on every ordinary run of this instrument and is MEASURED escaping every scored guard'. (d) I verified programmatically that neither the checker's SCOPE_STATEMENT constant nor the candidate's scopeStatement contains any of the eighteen variant identifiers the checker knows: zero hits on both.
centralClaimAdjudications.structuralRefusalAsShipped: verify_answer_provenance enforces scopeStatement verbatim against SCOPE_STATEMENT, and then runs the variant-name refusal over BOTH the candidate's text AND the checker's own constant, so re-listing variants in the constant is a finding this file produces about this file. I confirmed the loop exists and that the shipped text is clean under it.
centralClaimAdjudications.attackA_defeatTheSelfScan: SUCCEEDED, and this is a real weakness. The refusal is `if name in scope_text or name.split('-')[0] in scope_text.split()`. The second clause tokenises on WHITESPACE ONLY, so a bare variant prefix adjacent to punctuation is invisible to it. MEASURED against the shipped predicate: 'the variants AX6 and AX9 do exactly that' is FLAGGED; 'the variants AX6, AX9 and RX2c do exactly that' flags only AX9 and RX2c and MISSES 'AX6,'; '(AX6) and (AX9) do exactly that' is NOT FLAGGED AT ALL; 'variants AX6. AX9. RX2c. do exactly that' is NOT FLAGGED; 'the class is bounded by AX6/AX9/RX2c and nothing else' is NOT FLAGGED; 'only MD5-style regions escape' is NOT FLAGGED. So the exact sentence the predecessor was rejected for can be reintroduced with a comma or a bracket and the structural refusal stays silent. The checker's own comment says it 'refuses it structurally rather than by intention'; that is an overclaim for punctuated spellings. Recorded as IR-EP13-NB-02.
centralClaimAdjudications.attackB_narrowWithoutNamingAnything: SUCCEEDED, and it is the more fundamental of the two. I wrote a scope that names NO variant and is nevertheless the predecessor's false boundary in substance — 'NOT ESTABLISHED against a route region that reads or writes this guard's own stack frame, or the closure cells of the servers it installs. Against every other hostile route region the property IS established.' The self-scan reports zero hits on it. Editing the candidate alone is REJECTED by the verbatim rule; editing BOTH the candidate and the checker's own constant is GREEN. So the refusal prevents exactly one regression SHAPE — re-listing variant names — and prevents narrowing not at all. I record this as a limit on what the refusal buys and NOT as a defect, for two reasons: editing SCOPE_STATEMENT is editing the checker's own bytes, which this corpus has consistently held to be outside the threat model; and no published property rests on the refusal.
centralClaimAdjudications.whatDoesResistNarrowing: The parts that are measured rather than asserted. MEASURED: setting aNarrowingIsNotAClosure to false is REJECTED; dropping MD5 from escapedEveryGuard is REJECTED with both sets printed; dropping MD5 from declaredBlindSpotVariants is REJECTED; setting escapeSetIsAMeasurementNotACoverageClaim to false is REJECTED; setting anchoredToTheSeat to true is REJECTED; and a floated hiddenAnchoredObjectAgreements=21.0 is REJECTED against a measured 21. Most important, verify_evasion produces a finding IF A DECLARED ESCAPE IS EVER CAUGHT — 'Either the scope statement is understated or the variant no longer performs the discrimination it names' — so the disclosure of a live escape cannot be quietly retired by making the escape stop working.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: MD2 and MD3 — reproduce both directions with my own bytes
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: BOTH REPRODUCED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, EXACTLY AS CLAIMED
centralClaimAdjudications.howIBuiltThem: From the prose of ep12.review-independent.json IR-EP12-01 and from reading ServedLedger, ServedCall, LedgerWindow and _wrap in check-evaluation-proof-v10.py. I did not read the candidate's _MD2_OBSERVED / _MD3_OBSERVED strings until after mine were built and measured. My region builder asserts the text before # ROUTE-REGION-BEGIN and after # ROUTE-REGION-END is byte-identical to the base file before it writes.
centralClaimAdjudications.purity: asserted programmatically over my region text: none of _getframe, f_locals, f_back, f_globals, __closure__, cell_contents, __code__, __globals__, __traceback__, tb_frame, inspect, sys, importlib, getattr, setattr, vars, globals, __dict__, traceback, gc, ctypes, __builtins__, eval, exec, compile, __subclasses__ occurs. Zero impurities for SB-MD2, SB-MD3 and SB-MD6.
centralClaimAdjudications.againstThePredecessor: MEASURED. `python3 -I -B sb_md2.py evaluation-proof.v12.json` exits 0 and `sb_md3.py` exits 0, and the stdout of BOTH is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the unmodified check-evaluation-proof-v12.py's — sha256 38835c615a782c4d..., 5781 bytes, all three identical. The predecessor's blocking defect is real and I re-established it independently.
centralClaimAdjudications.againstV13: MEASURED. Both exit 1 with TWELVE findings each. Of those, SEVEN are A-9, one per pinned vector, reading 'with this guard's anchor installed BENEATH the seat — every binding the route region can read left byte-for-byte as it was at load time — the join returned an object THIS GUARD'S ANCHOR did not produce for this vector at depth 0 in that window (A-9)'. The remaining five are the aggregate 'hiddenAnchoredObjectAgreements=21; this run measured 14', 'not every answer-provenance rule held', and three own-constant-leaf-battery cascade findings. I extracted the rule ids from the sb_md3 run: the count is 7 x (A-9) and NOTHING ELSE. The claim that A-9 catches them ALONE is exact.
centralClaimAdjudications.assessment: This is the repair of IR-EP12-01 and it is precisely as advertised. The mechanism is right: A-2's window announces itself by changing the seat, A-9's does not change anything the region can read, and a region whose honesty is conditional on what it can read is therefore dishonest inside a window it cannot see.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: A-9 — attack the narrowing. Reach the hidden window, detect it, or find a fourth means
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: I COULD NOT REACH IT OR DEFEAT IT, IT FAILS CLOSED, AND I DID FIND A FOURTH MEANS OF DISTINGUISHING — which the scope covers, and which routes strictly more than the candidate's own published escape does.
centralClaimAdjudications.failsClosed: MEASURED. I disabled _seat_cells so the hidden window cannot be installed at all. Result: 39 findings, beginning 'this guard could not hold a HIDDEN anchored window over [check-c2-v4.py.canonical_plan_intent, check-c2-v4.py.plan_intent_commitment, check-c2-v4.py.validate_plan_intent] (A-9). A-9 is the only rule that measures a window the route region cannot see, and a rule that could not be evaluated is a finding, not an omission', plus a zero-record parity finding and three per-api A-9 findings per vector. An unevaluated A-9 is loud, not silent.
centralClaimAdjudications.myFourthMeans_SB_MD6: BUILT AND MEASURED. It compares NO BINDING AT ALL. It never looks at the seat, the declared accessor, the module object, the ledger's originals table, any closure cell, any frame or any dunder. It uses two facts: (i) the number of ledger entries a call produces separates the three cases, because plan_intent_commitment's internal canonical call re-enters the shared ledger when the load-time original runs it and does NOT when the guard's anchor runs it — I mapped this empirically with an instrumented region and measured the deltas as commit=2 unobserved, commit=1 inside the hidden window, commit=0 inside the visible window; and (ii) answer_provenance_guard drives the hidden window IMMEDIATELY after the visible one with no intervening call, so the join that follows a join served at the seat is the hidden one. SB-MD6 therefore answers honestly in the visible window (validate delta 0), honestly in the hidden window (previous join was served), and answers check-c2.py otherwise, repairing the ledger by rewriting the result field of the entry its own genuine call already created and deleting the entries its probe created.
centralClaimAdjudications.measuredOutcome: `python3 -I -B sb_md6.py evaluation-proof.v13.json` EXITS 0. Its stdout is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the honest run's — sha256 a160e3f4c8e87c576729..., 9118 bytes, compared programmatically. `python3 -I -B sb_md6.py --selftest` returns SELFTEST-PASS at exit 0. Every published number is unmoved, including the battery's 486/1152/1140/12, the evasion matrix, and every answer-provenance counter at 21/21/21/21/21/7/7/21/7 with the hidden trio at 21/7/7 and allRulesHeld true. My INDEPENDENT seat attribution — every reachable spelling of all three imported apis on both module objects and in the ledger's own originals table wrapped in retaining markers, driven in the production ordering, reading nothing either instrument publishes — reports: verdict {'check-c2.py': 7}, commitment {'check-c2.py': 7}, preimage {'check-c2.py': 7}, gate {'ACCEPT': 7}. The same harness against the UNMODIFIED checker reports {'check-c2-v4.py': 7} on all three. THE GATE IS ROUTED, not just the commitment.
centralClaimAdjudications.whyThisIsNotABlocker: Because the enforced, banner-printed boundary says so in advance and says so in the general form. SB-MD6 is a route region that can distinguish a call the guard is measuring from a call it is not, and that answers honestly whenever it judges itself observed. That is the class, verbatim. The scope also anticipates the specific means — 'counting the ledger entries its own call produces is a THIRD, and compares no binding at all' — and anticipates the general fact that I would find something it had not built: 'there are others this instrument has not thought of and cannot enumerate.' I looked hard for an escape OUTSIDE the class, i.e. a region that behaves IDENTICALLY observed and unobserved and still routes an answer, because that and only that would falsify the property rather than confirm the scope. I could not build one, and I believe the reason is structural: on this corpus the two encoders agree in VALUE at every position except four probe-family positions, so there is nothing to gain by answering differently except provenance, and provenance inside a guard-opened window is pinned by `witnessed.callee is anchors[api]` against a frame local the region cannot name.
centralClaimAdjudications.whatSB_MD6AddsThatMD5DoesNot: Severity. The candidate's MD5 substitutes plan_intent_commitment only, and RES-EP13-18 describes it as 'routing every pinned commitment to the superseded encoder'. SB-MD6 routes the VALIDATION VERDICT — which IS the accept/reject gate, and which is where LB-C2-01 lives — as well as the commitment and the preimage. No sentence in v13 is falsified by that, because the scope is general and RES-EP13-16 says the outside-the-window answer is 'bound by value alone exactly as before'. But the one place a reader gets a CONCRETE sense of what the open class costs shows the weakest instance of it. Recorded as IR-EP13-NB-01.
otherThingsIAttackedAndFailedToBreak: reaching the anchor object: it is a frame local of answer_provenance_guard and a closure cell of the servers; I found no path to it that is not a frame read or a cell read
making a substitute object pass `is`: impossible without the anchor
displacing the hidden install mid-window: _hidden_anchored checks cell.cell_contents is served at exit and reports a displaced cell as a finding

probing the commitment from inside c2_validate_intent to get the signal earlier: the probe call is served by the anchored server inside either window and appends a fourth witness record, which breaks the exactly-one-per-api-at-depth-0 parity of A-8 and A-9. This is why SB-MD6 has to infer the hidden window positionally instead, and it is a real cost the design imposes on the attacker

poisoning the anchor instance's module globals: _function_bindings pins every FunctionType binding and moved_anchors pins the anchor object and its code object, so validate_plan_intent, _validate_plan_intent, canonical_plan_intent and _normalise_json are all covered

centralClaimAdjudications.title: Residual padding — try to gut one
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: I COULD NOT GUT ONE OF ITS MEANING. The anchor-stub attack still passes, and the stub IS the disclosure. The contradictory-prose attack passes and is DISCLOSED by the residual that is itself anchored on that sentence.
centralClaimAdjudications.vaguePadding: MEASURED over ALL NINETEEN residuals, not a sample: replacing each residual's text with grammatical prose that satisfies its declared minimum length and says nothing is REJECTED 19 times out of 19. The claim reproduces exactly.
centralClaimAdjudications.anchorDamage: MEASURED, ten attacks on RES-EP13-18 (the residual that discloses my own escape's class). REJECTED: dropping either anchor; PARAPHRASING an anchor rather than dropping it; dropping the bound value text; truncating to minimum-1 characters; an empty text; anchors with no bound value; bound value with no anchors. Nine of ten refused, each by a finding that quotes the missing sentence.
centralClaimAdjudications.anchorStubStillPasses: MEASURED and GREEN for RES-EP13-18, -02, -16, -19, -15 and -12 — I reduced each to its anchors plus 'MEASURED ON THIS RUN: <bound value>' plus meaningless padding to the minimum. But this is a materially different outcome from v12's. I measured the fraction of each stub that is VERBATIM DISCLOSURE — anchors plus bound value over total length — at 92% for RES-EP13-18, 94% for RES-EP13-02, 93% for RES-EP13-16, 95% for RES-EP13-12, 71% for RES-EP13-19 and 65% for RES-EP13-15. Under v12 the anchors were short tokens like 'ROUTE REGION' and 'AX6' and a stub carried no information at all; here a gutted RES-EP13-18 still says, verbatim, that A-9's hidden window is not invisible to a region that counts the ledger entries its own call produces and that the anchor's internal calls do not re-enter the shared ledger. The attack no longer removes the meaning.
centralClaimAdjudications.contradictoryProse: SUCCEEDS. I kept both anchors and the bound value intact and padded with 'None of the above is actually a limitation in practice: the hidden window closes the class completely, no region can escape it, and the escape described above has never been observed and cannot occur.' GREEN, zero findings. This is exactly what RES-EP13-19 concedes in its own enforced anchor — 'This does not stop an author writing the anchors and then padding them with contradictory prose, and no mechanical rule inside a checker can; binding is not meaning' — and I confirmed that dropping THAT anchor is itself rejected. A disclosed limitation, disclosed in the right place, with the disclosure structurally protected.
centralClaimAdjudications.substanceRuleIsSelfMeasured: residual_substance() measures the checker's OWN table and publishes it; 5073 anchor characters across 19 residuals, 0 below 55% of their declared minimum, and I confirmed both the totalAnchorChars and the substancePercentRequired are rejected when edited.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: Float / bool sweep — my own, not the candidate's battery
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: UPHELD DIGIT FOR DIGIT. The candidate's disclosure of this class is exactly right.
centralClaimAdjudications.method: My own sweep on the harder protocol. I injected float(n) at every INTEGER leaf — same value, different type, invisible to a bare `!=` — and the corresponding bool at every leaf whose value is 0 or 1, then ran the WHOLE checking layer per case against a primed authority with the top-level exit-matrix and battery probes suppressed and their counterparts seeded, so the only difference from a full run is that the battery does not re-enter itself. Baseline with an unmutated candidate: ZERO findings. Every rejection classified BY READING THE FINDING TEXT, not by exit code.
centralClaimAdjudications.measurement: 180 integer leaves, 306 boolean leaves (180+306 = 486, equal to the published intBoolLeaves), 198 cases. ADMITTED with zero findings: 4. Rejected by a finding that NAMES THE POSITION: 148. Rejected by a type-exact whole-block strict_equal that names the BLOCK: 46. Rejected by contract-root census arithmetic alone: 0. No boolean admitted at any position.
centralClaimAdjudications.theFourAdmitted: $.astScanScope.ownConstantLeafBattery.intBoolLeaves, .cases, .rejected and .silentlyAdmitted, all as floats. Those four are EXACTLY the four positions the candidate publishes in silentlyAdmittedPositions, and RES-EP13-10 states the mechanism and is declared TEXT-ONLY rather than given a test that would pass on hollow text. My sweep found the disclosed set and nothing else.
centralClaimAdjudications.onTheNonZeroExits: I took the brief's warning seriously and did not treat a non-zero exit as evidence a guard fired. The 46 whole-block rejections are genuine TYPE catches — strict_equal is recursive and type-exact, so 21.0 for 21 and False for 0 fail at those positions — but the message names the block rather than the leaf. That is IR-EP12-NB-07 restated and it is unchanged at 46 of 198. Zero cases were rejected only by census arithmetic, which is the shape that makes a collateral rejection worthless.
centralClaimAdjudications.corpusContext: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE 7.4 records this class across the corpus, including check-trusted-request-context-v3.py at 100% of its integer leaves and check-r1-v1.5.py at 40 of 52 boolean positions. v13's own checking layer does not carry that class: its comparisons are strict_equal or _exact_int throughout and the only positions it admits are the four it publishes.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: The RES-EP12-11 correction
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: V13 IS RIGHT AND THE PREDECESSOR REVIEWER WAS RIGHT; v12 was wrong and RET-EP13-06 correctly retracts it.
centralClaimAdjudications.measured: I ran check-completeness.py on today's bytes. It exits 1 and prints BOTH: the C-2 surface row carries 'open: IR-C2V4-01' and pulls 'seal readiness: 8/11', and separately 'cross-cutting open findings: 1' / 'open: R2-FINAL-03'. The exit condition at line 328 is `ok = (shape_complete == len(rows) and reviewed_complete == len(rows) and seal_ready == len(rows) and not cross['openIds'] and not errors)`, so seal_ready and the cross-cutting open set are independent terms and EACH ALONE drives exit 1. check-completeness.py contains ZERO occurrences of 'IR-C2V4-01' and ZERO of 'R2-FINAL-03', so both are scanned from artifacts rather than hard-coded, which is why both can be open at once.
centralClaimAdjudications.assessment: RES-EP13-11 states this correctly — 'the cause did not move, a second cause was added' — and RET-EP13-06 retracts v12's contrary claim by name. It remains correctly declared TEXT-ONLY, because the instrument still has no in-process measurement of another checker's exit code, and inventing one that would pass on hollow text is the thing this corpus refuses.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: Preserved work

A green check() therefore IS the verification that published equals measured, and I confirmed by mutation that these positions are not baked in.

centralClaimAdjudications.theObjectAnchor: The thing the v12 reviewer could not break, I also could not break. A seat is a binding; the anchor is a function object held in a guard frame local and in the servers' closure cells; the server reads the cell into a local, calls the local and RECORDS the local, so a rewritten cell yields a record naming the substitute rather than a record that lies. Every seat rewrite, wrap, replay and module-accessor spelling in the battery is caught and answer provenance is the sole scored catcher for ten of them.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: THE RULING — is this an acceptable terminus or a fifth rejection?
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: AN ACCEPTABLE TERMINUS. I rule for acceptance, and I do so as the reviewer who routed the gate.
centralClaimAdjudications.theQuestionPutToMe: Does the honest publication of a live escape make the green banner readable, or does a green exit with 7/7 wrong-module answers remain unacceptable regardless?
centralClaimAdjudications.whereILand: It makes it readable. Here is the reasoning I commit to, in the order it decided me.
centralClaimAdjudications.one_whatIsActuallyBeingAdjudicated: Every escape in this chain — mine, MD2 through MD5, AX6, AX9, RX2c, RX1 — is built by REWRITING THIRTY-ONE LINES OF THE CHECKER'S OWN SOURCE. A checker cannot defend against arbitrary modification of itself; the v12 reviewer said so explicitly and I agree without reservation. So 'a green exit while the answers are wrong' cannot be the standard, because it is reachable against ANY instrument by construction. The question this corpus has actually been adjudicating for five rounds is narrower and correct: IS THE INSTRUMENT'S PUBLISHED ACCOUNT OF ITS OWN LIMITS TRUE? On that question v9 failed (an AST scan was the sole guard for a property), v10 failed (the ledger proved a call, not an answer), v11 failed (the anchor was a seat the region owned), v12 failed (the scope was an enumeration and I falsified it by building outside it). v13 does not fail it. I attacked the account with the strongest region I could build and the account held.
centralClaimAdjudications.two_theBannerSentenceIsTrue: The banner does not say 'the answers are right'. It says 'ANSWER PROVENANCE ESTABLISHED, WITHIN THE SCOPE PRINTED ON THE NEXT LINE AND ENFORCED VERBATIM', and the next line is the characterisation. The property itself is worded 'Inside a window this guard opens'. Under SB-MD6 that sentence is literally TRUE: inside all fourteen anchored windows per vector — seven visible, seven hidden — the twenty-one answers ARE the anchor's own objects, because SB-MD6 is honest exactly there. What SB-MD6 falsifies is a claim the document does not make.
centralClaimAdjudications.three_theDisclosureIsEnforcedNotIntended: This is what separates v13 from a document that merely admits a weakness in prose. The live escape is BUILT AND EXECUTED on every ordinary run; it is in DECLARED_ESCAPES; the measured escape set must equal the declared escape set IN BOTH DIRECTIONS; aNarrowingIsNotAClosure must be true; escapeSetIsAMeasurementNotACoverageClaim must be true; and — the sharpest of them — verify_evasion produces a finding IF A DECLARED ESCAPE IS EVER CAUGHT, so the disclosure cannot be retired by quietly breaking the variant that carries it. I tested each of those five by mutation and each is rejected. A disclosure that the instrument is required to keep DEMONSTRATING is a different object from a caveat.
centralClaimAdjudications.four_theScopeIsNotVacuouslyBroad: A boundary stated as 'by any means whatever' could be a way of claiming nothing. It is not, here, because the POSITIVE residue is precise, testable and load-bearing: inside a window this guard opens, the answer IS the anchor's object, compared by `is` against a frame local. That residue is the sole scored catcher for ten built variants — AX2, AX4, AX8, MD2, MD3, MD4, RX1, RX3, RX4, RX6 — and it is what makes A-9 catch the exact regions that defeated the predecessor. The scope narrows the claim; it does not empty it.
centralClaimAdjudications.five_theCostOfRejecting: I asked myself what a v14 would have to do to clear a fifth rejection on this ground, because a standard nobody can meet is not a standard. Closing the class means removing the region's ABILITY to profit from discrimination, not its ability to discriminate — the natural spelling is to keep the guard's anchored servers installed for every C-2 call the checker acts on, so that there is no unobserved window to be dishonest in, at the cost of A-7. That is the v12 reviewer's clearance option (a), it is not obviously impossible, and v13 did not take it. But — and this decided me — v13 NOWHERE CLAIMS THE CLASS IS UNCLOSABLE. I searched the candidate for it: 'closab', 'cannot be closed', 'never could be', 'whole drive', 'unobserved window' all return ZERO occurrences. The only such sentence in the checker is inside a SELFTEST_MUTATIONS string that the selftest REJECTS. What v13 claims is exactly and only that A-9 is a narrowing and not a closure, and that claim is TRUE and MEASURED. Rejecting an artifact for failing to close a hole it never claimed to close, when it measures the hole, publishes the hole, exercises the hole on every run and is structurally forbidden from pretending the hole shut, would be rejecting it for the sin of accuracy.
centralClaimAdjudications.six_noVerdictMoves: SB-MD6, like MD2, MD3 and MD5, routes the four divergent positions honestly, so all seven gates remain ACCEPT and the commitment and preimage are unchanged. The defect I demonstrated is in PROVENANCE, and provenance outside a guard-opened window is precisely what the scope disclaims. This review therefore establishes nothing about whether v13 reaches a wrong verdict on today's pinned bytes, and I do not claim it does.
centralClaimAdjudications.whatIWouldNotAccept: I want the boundary of my own ruling on the record, because it is narrow. I am NOT ruling that any weakness becomes acceptable once disclosed. I would have rejected this artifact if the enforced scope had been false, as v12's was — and I tested that first and hardest. I would have rejected it if the disclosure had been prose the checker does not enforce, or if the escape had been asserted rather than built, or if the escape could be retired without a finding, or if a single sentence in the enforced or printed surface had claimed the class was bounded. None of those is the case. What I am ruling is that an instrument may publish a property it has genuinely established, beside a characterisation of the class it has genuinely NOT established, provided the characterisation is stated by capability, is enforced verbatim, is printed where the reader looks, is not contradicted by anything the checker verifies, and is accompanied by a live instance the instrument is required to keep running. v13 meets all five.
centralClaimAdjudications.theOneThingIWouldFixBeforeV14: The two blocks the checker does not verify — assurance.nonClaims and guardInventory.whatNoGuardHereCovers — still speak in the predecessor's voice. nonClaims says the scope is 'a route region that reaches this guard's frame defeats it' and that the escape set is 'a measurement over twenty-five built classes' when this run builds and publishes twenty-nine; whatNoGuardHereCovers names ONLY the frame-and-cell class as the declared uncovered region, does not mention the observability class or MD5 at all, repeats the stale 'twenty-five', and cites RES-EP12-15 where it means RES-EP13-15. That is not the v12 defect — nothing there claims the property IS established outside the named set, there is a catch-all bullet, and the enforced scope carries an override clause binding the whole document — but it is the same voice, in the two places a checker that greps its own claims does not reach. Add both blocks to the enforced set and the last echo of IR-EP12-01 goes with them.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The open class is disclosed at its WEAKEST reachable severity: the published instance routes the commitment, and a region of the same class routes the GATE
nonBlockingObservations.observation: RES-EP13-18 describes the live escape as MD5 'routing every pinned commitment to the superseded encoder', and MD5 as built substitutes plan_intent_commitment only. I built SB-MD6 in the same class, by the same means — the ledger-entry-count signal, comparing no binding at all — and it routes the VALIDATION VERDICT, the commitment AND the preimage, 7 of 7 each, to check-c2.py, with exit 0 and a banner byte-identical to the honest run's and --selftest SELFTEST-PASS. The verdict IS the accept/reject gate; A-5 exists precisely because 'c2_join returns early on any finding, so a verdict substitution decides admission by itself'; and LB-C2-01, the defect this whole chain exists to measure, lives in the verdict. NOTHING PUBLISHED IS FALSIFIED BY THIS: SCOPE_STATEMENT is general and covers it, RES-EP13-16 says the outside-window answer is 'bound by value alone exactly as before', and the escape set is declared a measurement over instances. But a reader pricing the residual reads RES-EP13-18, and RES-EP13-18 shows them a commitment substitution. Building an OBSERVABILITY_ESCAPES member that routes the verdict — SB-MD6 or the author's own spelling — would cost the same as MD5 and would price the residual honestly. This is the sharpest observation in this review and it is the one I would most want a v14 to act on.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The scope self-scan is defeated by punctuation, and cannot detect narrowing at all; 'refuses it structurally rather than by intention' is an overclaim
nonBlockingObservations.observation: verify_answer_provenance scans both the candidate's scopeStatement and the checker's own SCOPE_STATEMENT for every variant identifier, using `name in scope_text or name.split('-')[0] in scope_text.split()`. The second clause tokenises on WHITESPACE ONLY. MEASURED against the shipped predicate: 'the variants AX6 and AX9 do exactly that' is flagged, but '(AX6) and (AX9) do exactly that', 'variants AX6. AX9. RX2c. do exactly that', 'the class is bounded by AX6/AX9/RX2c and nothing else' and 'only MD5-style regions escape' are NOT flagged, and in 'the variants AX6, AX9 and RX2c do exactly that' the comma hides AX6 while AX9 and RX2c are caught. So the predecessor's own rejected sentence can be reintroduced with a comma. Separately and more fundamentally, the refusal is NAME-based, so it cannot see narrowing: I wrote a scope naming no variant at all that is v12's false boundary in substance ('NOT ESTABLISHED against a route region that reads or writes this guard's own stack frame, or the closure cells of the servers it installs. Against every other hostile route region the property IS established'), the self-scan reports zero hits, and with both the candidate and the checker's constant edited the run is GREEN. NON-BLOCKING because editing SCOPE_STATEMENT is editing the checker's own bytes, which this corpus holds outside the threat model, and because no published property rests on the refusal. Stripping punctuation before tokenising is a one-line fix; the narrowing gap is not closable by a grep and should be described as what it is.

nonBlockingObservations.title: answerProvenance.independentPathIsUnreachable is FALSE by measurement: 75 private instances, including the anchor and the reference, are left in sys.modules
nonBlockingObservations.observation: The candidate states 'Reaching any of it requires this guard's frame or a server's closure cell, which is RES-EP12-02 and is measured.' MEASURED: after a single heavy_measurements run, sys.modules carries SEVENTY-FIVE entries whose names begin '_ep13', among them _ep13_anchor_2_check_c2_v4_py, _ep13_anchor3_3_check_c2_py and _ep13_reference_4_check_c2_v4_py. _exec_verified does `sys.modules[name] = module` with a predictable prefix and nothing ever deletes them. sys.modules is neither this guard's frame nor a server's closure cell, so the sentence is false and the reader's exclusion set is incomplete. The string 'sys.modules' does not occur anywhere in the candidate, and v13 lists IR-EP12-NB-04 in nonBlockingObservationsAddressed while leaving the reachability and both of its named consequences unchanged: A-8's binding check still filters on isinstance(value, types.FunctionType) so the anchored instance's non-function globals are unchecked, and the A-1 REFERENCE instance still has NO integrity check of any kind. NON-BLOCKING for three measured reasons: the field is not enforced by the checker (zero occurrences of 'independentPathIsUnreachable' in check-evaluation-proof-v13.py) and is not printed in the banner; the introspection tripwire enumerates sys, importlib and __import__ so the cheap spellings exit 1; and I could not turn the reachability into an escape — moved_anchors pins the anchor object and its code object, anchorInstanceBindingsUnmoved pins every FunctionType binding including _validate_plan_intent and _normalise_json, and on this corpus the two encoders agree in value at every non-probe position so poisoning a reachable instance changes nothing worth changing. Deleting each private module from sys.modules after _exec_verified returns, extending the binding check to the reference instance, and restating the sentence to name the three reach paths as instances rather than as an exhaustive set would close it.
nonBlockingObservations.measuredBy: r13/harness.py driving heavy_measurements and enumerating sys.modules

nonBlockingObservations.title: assurance.nonClaims and guardInventory.whatNoGuardHereCovers are NOT enforced by the checker and still carry the predecessor's narrow framing and two stale counts
nonBlockingObservations.observation: Neither block appears anywhere in check-evaluation-proof-v13.py — zero occurrences of 'nonClaims' and zero of 'whatNoGuardHereCovers' — so both are unverified prose in a document whose thesis is that a prose assertion is not a record. What they say: nonClaims[2] 'the escape set is a measurement over TWENTY-FIVE built classes' where evasionMeasurement.variantsBuilt is 29 and is enforced at 29; nonClaims[3] 'the answer-provenance property is scoped and the scope is printed in the banner: A ROUTE REGION THAT REACHES THIS GUARD'S FRAME DEFEATS IT', which is the predecessor's framing verbatim in substance; whatNoGuardHereCovers bullet 2 names ONLY 'a route region that reads or writes this guard's stack frame or its servers' closure cells: DECLARED, built as AX6, AX9 and RX2c' and does not mention the observability class or MD5 at all, although MD5 is a declared escape measured escaping every scored guard on this same run; bullet 4 repeats 'any evasion class not among the TWENTY-FIVE built here'; bullet 3 cites 'RES-EP12-15' where it means RES-EP13-15. I considered this at length as a candidate blocker and rejected it. It is NOT the v12 defect, for three measured reasons: nothing here makes the universal claim v12 made — no sentence says the property IS established outside the named set; bullet 4 is a catch-all that covers the gap in intent even with the wrong number; and the ENFORCED, banner-printed SCOPE_STATEMENT carries an override clause that binds this document — 'EVERY VARIANT NAMED ANYWHERE IN THIS DOCUMENT IS AN INSTANCE OF THAT CLASS AND IS NEVER ITS DEFINITION'. It is nevertheless the last echo of IR-EP12-01 in this artifact, it sits in the two places the checker's own grep does not reach, and it is three edits and one _expect from being correct.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Contradictory prose around intact anchors still passes, and the whole-block rejection message still names the block
nonBlockingObservations.observation: Two disclosed limitations I re-measured rather than took on trust. (a) A residual whose anchors and bound value are intact but whose surrounding prose CONTRADICTS them passes green; I built one for RES-EP13-18 that says 'the hidden window closes the class completely, no region can escape it' and got zero findings. RES-EP13-19 concedes this in an anchor that is itself enforced, and dropping that anchor is rejected, so the concession is structurally protected — which is why this is MINOR rather than MAJOR. (b) 46 of the 198 cases in my float/bool sweep are rejected by a type-exact whole-block strict_equal whose message names the BLOCK rather than the leaf (answerProvenance.positiveControl, predecessorDefeatControl, secondPredecessorDefeatControl, preservedMeasurements sub-blocks). No case escapes, so this is message granularity; but the corpus standard is that a rejection should name the position it rejects, and a future auditor grepping finding text will not find those leaves named. Unchanged from IR-EP12-NB-07.

nonBlockingObservations.title: An attacker cost the design imposes, worth recording because it is the one place A-9 bites harder than the scope admits
nonBlockingObservations.observation: Recorded in the candidate's favour. A-8 and A-9 both require EXACTLY ONE witness record per imported api per window, all at depth 0, all over this vector's fingerprint. That makes the obvious strengthening of MD5 — probe the commitment from inside c2_validate_intent to get the observation signal before the verdict is returned — impossible, because inside either anchored window the probe is served by the guard's own server and appends a fourth record. SB-MD6 has to infer the hidden window POSITIONALLY instead (the hidden join is the one immediately after a join served at the seat), which is a strictly more fragile signal that a reordering of the two drives, or an extra join between them, would break. So the record-parity rule is doing real work against this class that neither the scope nor RES-EP13-18 claims credit for, and a v14 that shuffles or interleaves the visible and hidden drives per vector would raise the cost of my own attack materially without changing any published property.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: CPython 3.14.6 (main, Jun 10 2026) [Clang 21.0.0], Darwin 25.5.0 arm64, `python3 -I -B`, stdlib only. There is no `timeout` binary on this host. Ordinary v13 run 54 s in an isolated lab; --selftest ~50 s; check-c2-v6.py ~81 s as declared. My lab is a fresh directory holding a byte-identical copy of the 33 pinned inputs plus the candidate and the checker (35 files); the unmodified checker exits 0 there. My in-process sweep harness suppresses only the top-level exit-matrix and own-constant-leaf probes (_NESTED[0]=1) and seeds their two counterparts, and I confirmed the unmutated candidate scores ZERO findings under it before using it for anything. docs/coop is untracked, so pre-existence of the two dependent failures was established BY CAUSE and by execution, not against git HEAD. Other lanes are writing in this directory during this review; every digest in verifiedInputs was recomputed by me at the time I used it, and the two subjects were re-hashed again immediately before this file was written.
